scope: Rename archive, per-open deferred change time, file-wide close notifications and persistent recovery. Full SMB/NFS remains unfinished.

checks: four signed/encrypted dialects set archive immediately, preserve creation/access/write times and defer change time plus one attribute notification to close
explicit change time stays frozen across repeated rename and close while a real archive change is notified once at the final name
explicit time after rename cancels its deferred update; -2 re-enables it without inventing archive changes
another close flushes file-wide pending notifications while only the originating open completes its deferred timestamp
directory rename updates change time at close without applying a data-file archive bit
SMB process loss recovers durable rename metadata; offline backup refuses unresolved markers and succeeds after file-service restart recovery
recovery discards stale rename markers without transferring metadata to a replacement native incarnation
SMB2.1/3.0/3.0.2/3.1.1 signed/encrypted asynchronous create/rename/delete, live ECHO, CANCEL and CLOSE cleanup
per-open first filter/watch-tree settings, FIFO completion and events buffered between requests
native host writes trigger recursive watches while nonrecursive watches ignore descendants
rapid service-created recursive subtrees retain every ordered directory/file event between requests without requiring a rescan
recursive file/directory cross-parent moves report REMOVED/ADDED, same-parent renames report OLD/NEW and moved subtrees retain native coverage
events buffered across service operations remain byte-bounded, overflow without a partial batch and resume from fresh changes
recursive watches stop observing moved-out subtrees and do not disclose queued outside names
SIZE filter ignores equal-length writes and reports actual growth
LAST_WRITE observes new-file writes even when native CREATE and WRITE are drained together
first per-open zero/short capacity persists, reopening restores capacity; NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR has no partial records; invalid-only filters stay pending and cancel cleanly
directory/list-access validation and persistent shared security descriptor changes generate SECURITY notifications
portable DOS attributes, creation-time and EA changes participate in native notification streams
initial CREATE metadata produces only ADDED; subsequent changes still produce MODIFIED
recursive descriptor exhaustion stays visibly overflowed across requests and releases all watches on close
delete-pending directories complete outstanding watches without waiting for last-handle deletion
TREE_DISCONNECT and LOGOFF finish pending notifications with NOTIFY_CLEANUP before releasing keys
policy revocation denies the pending poll, invalidates its old handle and permits a fresh exclusive read open without retained watch/sharing authority
schema 6 upgrades to 7 with backups in every file worker
four signed/encrypted dialects: per-open mode, last-close unlink, nonempty directory preservation, explicit disposition, notifications and rename
killed SMB worker recovers durable intents, deletes files/empty directories and preserves nonempty directories without restarting other services
offline metadata backup accepts schema 7, refuses unresolved close intents and succeeds after recovery
CREATE/QUERY/SET persistent DOS attributes, zero/no-change and NORMAL semantics; readonly open/delete checks and granted-handle authority
four independent timestamps, native mtime, zero/no-change, per-handle explicit/-1 freeze and -2 re-enable; invalid times reject before attribute mutation
binary extended attributes on CREATE/QUERY/SET, case-insensitive updates, deletion, restart, NEED_EA and access rights; malformed chains reject atomically
attributes follow native object across rename/restart, directory invariants hold, replacement object does not inherit stale metadata
per-open mode CREATE/QUERY/SET and FileAllInformation agreement, write-through writes, independent handles, invalid synchronous/immutable modes and SMB2 ignored synchronous CREATE flags
EA cursor paging, restart, single-entry and explicit indexes, independent opens, bounded whole-entry overflow and undersized-buffer retries
selected-name EA queries preserve request order and scan cursor, ignore index/restart, match case-insensitively, return absent names, bound output and reject malformed chains without cursor changes
MxAc maximal access uses fresh policy and readonly restrictions, supports optional change-time comparison and chained QFid replies, rejects malformed/duplicate contexts before mutation
EA writes atomically update change time/archive while respecting frozen timestamps; exact 65531-byte aggregate limit and standard invalid-name/list statuses

limitations: No power-loss atomicity claim across native rename and subsequent SQL metadata commit.
Full notification batching/filtering, stream events, leases/oplocks and durable opens remain open.
